version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm/vmscan: reclaim every zone in per-node proactive reclaim

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch modifies the per-node proactive reclaim function to scan every zone, not just ZONE_NORMAL, in order to reclaim movable memory as well. This addresses a problem where nodes with only movable memory were not being reclaimed properly. The approach taken is to change the `reclaim_idx` field of the `scan_control` structure to always set it to the maximum number of zones, allowing all zones to be scanned.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] mm/page_alloc: let the highest memory node recover from hopeless state

version_history.subject: [PATCH] mm/page_alloc: let the highest memory node recover from hopeless state

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch fixes a problem where the highest memory node in a system cannot recover from a 'hopeless' state, even when its zone recovers above the high watermark. The issue arises because the current code checks if there is another memory node available for allocations to fall back to by looking at the next higher-numbered node ID, which always returns false for the highest node. This patch changes the check to count the number of nodes with a state of N_MEMORY, effectively checking if any other node exists. As a result, the highest node can now recover from its hopeless state and kswapd will be re-enabled.

review_comments.author: Zi Yan
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Zi Yan questioned the dependency of clearing kswapd's hopeless state on a static memory topology, arguing that it should be reset regardless of available fallback nodes, as kswapd can go hopeless later if reclamation fails.
review_comments.raw_body:
Why does a runtime behavior, clearing kswapd hopeless state, depend on a
static memory topology (excluding memory hotadd/hotremove in this
context)? There is nothing telling us if a fallback node has available memory.

Just reset it regardless. kswapd can go hopeless later if the node
cannot be reclaimed.

BTW, LLM also points out that kswapd_try_clear_hopeless(), called by
direct reclaim, only clears hopeless when the node is balanced, but that
rarely happens. So hopeless state can stay much longer if there is only
one node. Adding Jiayuna, who added kswapd_try_clear_hopeless(), to gvie
some insight.

This led to stale entries being used by reclaimers between node regaining memory and its targets being rebuilt. The patch resets the targets of every node, fixing this issue.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 1/5] mm/page_alloc: detect zonelist rebuilds from memory hot-add
series_items.patch_summary: This patch detects and handles zonelist rebuilds caused by memory hot-add, which can lead to spurious allocation failures for __GFP_THISNODE callers. The issue arises when onlining a zone's first block rewrites the zonelists in place, causing concurrent allocations to fail. To fix this, the patch gates sequence checks on CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTPLUG instead of just CONFIG_MEMORY_HOTREMOVE, ensuring that all configurations that rebuild zonelists after boot are covered.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 2/5] mm/page_alloc: validate zonelist slots against concurrent rebuilds
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a concurrency issue in the Linux kernel's page allocation system. When a zone is being rebuilt online, it can shift all zonelist slots after the new zone, potentially causing a previously filtered zone to be used by an in-flight walk. To fix this, the patch adds a validation step to recheck the loaded zone against the highest zone index and nodemask in both allocator loops. This ensures that only valid zones are used during allocation, preventing potential crashes or data corruption. The patch also includes a minor optimization by sharing cacheline access with an existing load.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 3/5] mm/page_alloc: snapshot the preferred zone against shrink rebuilds
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the `get_page_from_freelist` function to read the preferred zone only once, rather than at every use. This is done to prevent a kernel NULL pointer dereference that can occur when a concurrent zonelist rebuild replaces or nulls out the preferred slot. The change ensures that even if the preferred slot is replaced, a stale but valid zone will still be used, preventing the dereference error.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 4/5] mm/page_alloc: keep a zone's pagesets when it goes empty
series_items.patch_summary: This patch prevents the freeing of a zone's pagesets when it goes empty, which can lead to memory corruption and leaks. The pagesets are kept for the life of the zone, similar to pgdat->per_cpu_nodestats, and only folded in during zone_pcp_reset(). This change is necessary because setup_zone_pageset() now reuses existing pagesets and zone_pcp_init() keeps them when a node is re-added. The patch addresses an issue introduced by commit 340175b7d14d, which freed the pagesets when a zone became empty.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v2 5/5] mm/mmzone: read each zoneref slot once when filtering by nodemask
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the performance of the __next_zones_zonelist() function by reading each zoneref slot only once when filtering by nodemask. The original code read the slot twice, which could lead to a NULL pointer dereference when offlining a zone's last block and rebuilding the zonelists in place. The patch fixes this issue by testing the zone directly after reading the slot, and it also removes unnecessary inline functions and simplifies the code.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series addresses five races in the Linux memory allocator related to memory hotplug. The issues arise when multiple CPUs are updating state simultaneously, leading to potential crashes or incorrect behavior. The patches fix problems with zonelists being rebuilt by memory hotplug, pagesets of a zone being emptied, and offlining a zone's last block. They also address issues with the allocator using zones that have been filtered out and dereferencing NULL pointers in certain situations. The patches were tested on a QEMU guest with three NUMA nodes and a cold-plugged DIMM left offline at boot.

version_history.subject: [PATCH nfs-utils] mountd: fetch root filehandles over netlink

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch modifies the mountd service in nfs-utils to fetch root filehandles over netlink instead of relying on /proc/fs/nfsd/filehandle. It introduces a new command, NFSD_CMD_FILEHANDLE_GET, which is used first to retrieve the filehandle from the kernel's cache. If this fails or if the kernel does not support the new command, it falls back to using /proc/fs/nfsd/filehandle as before. The patch also updates the configure probe to require the new command and attributes in nfsd_netlink.h.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH] nfsd: add NFSD_CMD_FILEHANDLE_GET for root filehandle lookup

version_history.subject: [PATCH] nfsd: add NFSD_CMD_FILEHANDLE_GET for root filehandle lookup

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch adds a new netlink command, NFSD_CMD_FILEHANDLE_GET, to the NFS server (nfsd) that allows clients to look up the root filehandle of an export for a specific client domain. The command takes three parameters: the client domain name, the path of the export, and the maximum size of the filehandle that can be accepted by the client. The patch also includes a kselftest to validate the new command's behavior and ensure it matches the existing /proc/fs/nfsd/filehandle transaction interface used by rpc.mountd. A companion patch for nfs-utils will be forthcoming.

review_comments.author: Chuck Lever
review_comments.summary: Reviewer noted four technical issues: the selftest's proc_filehandle() function fails to parse the /proc reply due to a prefixing issue, the new binary is missing from .gitignore, the code silently clamps handle size to NFS3_FHSIZE instead of capping it at maxsize as claimed in the yaml doc and kernel-doc, and fh_proc_mount() leaves self->mnt behind when mount(2) fails after mkdir() succeeds.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Jeff, thanks for the patch. Review findings:

1. The selftest's proc_filehandle() cannot parse the /proc reply.
   write_filehandle() emits the handle via qword_addhex(), which
   prefixes the hex digits with "\x" (net/sunrpc/cache.c), so the
   first hexval() call fails and the function returns -EIO.

2. The new binary is missing from tools/testing/selftests/nfsd/
   .gitignore, unlike the four sibling programs listed there.

3. The yaml doc for maxsize and the kernel-doc claim the handle is
   capped at @maxsize, but the code silently clamps to NFS3_FHSIZE.
   A caller passing 128 gets a 64-byte handle with no error.

4. My sashiko instance here noted that fh_proc_mount() leaves
   self->mnt behind when mount(2) fails after mkdir() succeeds, so
   teardown's rmdir() of the tmpdir fails.

Can you send a v2 that addresses these issues?


-- 
Chuck Lever (Come to NFS bake-a-thon! https://nfsv4bat.org)
